section_summary: This section (pages 81–91) of State Department decimal file 894.0011 documents diplomatic exchanges and protocol concerning the Japanese Imperial Family between 1934 and 1935. It primarily details the official communications surrounding the birth and naming of Prince Akihito, including Emperor Hirohito's formal announcement, President Franklin D. Roosevelt's congratulatory reply transmitted via Ambassador Joseph C. Grew, and related State Department correspondence. The section also includes a 1934 cross-reference sheet concerning the visit of Prince Tsunenori and Princess Toshiko to Stockholm and an internal 1935 Far Eastern Affairs memorandum regarding diplomatic felicitations on imperial births.

subfiles.about: Emperor Hirohito informs President Roosevelt of the birth of his son, Prince Akihito, on December 23, 1933.
subfiles.summary: Emperor Hirohito officially notifies President Franklin D. Roosevelt that Empress Nagako was delivered of an imperial prince on December 23, 1933, who was given the name Akihito on December 29. The Emperor conveys his unchanging friendship and expresses full confidence that the President will share in the imperial family's joy on this auspicious occasion. The document consists of the concluding Japanese text dated February 5, 1934, along with its official English translation.
subfiles.title: Letter from Emperor Hirohito to President Franklin D. Roosevelt Announcing the Birth of Prince Akihito, with Translation

subfiles.about: The Department of State instructs Ambassador Grew to deliver President Roosevelt's congratulatory letter to Emperor Hirohito and lodge an office copy with the Foreign Office.
subfiles.summary: Under Secretary of State William Phillips transmits to Ambassador Joseph C. Grew in Tokyo the original and an office copy of an autographed letter from President Franklin D. Roosevelt addressed to Emperor Hirohito. Ambassador Grew is instructed to transmit the office copy to the Japanese Foreign Office for its archives and convey the original letter to the Emperor in an agreeable manner. The enclosed text of President Roosevelt's letter, dated March 28, 1934, congratulates the Emperor on the birth of Prince Akihito and extends wishes for the young prince's illustrious future.
subfiles.title: Instruction No. 508 from William Phillips to Joseph C. Grew, Transmitting President Roosevelt's Letter to Emperor Hirohito

subfiles.about: Acting Secretary Phillips informs the Japanese Ambassador that President Roosevelt has prepared an acknowledgment to Emperor Hirohito's announcement.
subfiles.summary: Acting Secretary of State William Phillips writes to Japanese Ambassador Hirosi Saito acknowledging receipt of the Ambassador's letter of March 26 transmitting an autographed letter from Emperor Hirohito. Phillips informs the Ambassador that the Emperor's announcement was submitted to President Roosevelt, who made a suitable acknowledgment. This acknowledgment has been forwarded to American Ambassador Joseph C. Grew in Tokyo for delivery to the Emperor.
subfiles.title: Letter from William Phillips to Japanese Ambassador Hirosi Saito

subfiles.about: Ambassador Grew reports the delivery of President Roosevelt's letter to the Japanese Foreign Office and encloses the diplomatic notes exchanged.
subfiles.summary: Ambassador Joseph C. Grew reports compliance with Department Instruction No. 508 regarding the conveyance of President Roosevelt's congratulatory letter to Emperor Hirohito. Grew addressed Note No. 237 on May 15, 1934, to Foreign Minister Kōki Hirota requesting that the letter be conveyed to the Emperor, and Hirota replied on May 18, 1934 (Note No. 54/P), confirming that steps had been taken to deliver the message. Copies of both diplomatic notes are enclosed with the despatch.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 799 from Joseph C. Grew to the Secretary of State, with Enclosures

subfiles.about: A cross-reference sheet noting Despatch No. 211 from Stockholm concerning the visit of Prince Tsunenori and Princess Toshiko to Sweden.
subfiles.summary: A Department of State Document File Note cross-referencing decimal file 858.00 P.R./112 for Despatch No. 211 from Stockholm. It records that Prince Tsunenori and Princess Toshiko of the Imperial Japanese Family arrived in Stockholm on July 21 with a large suite. In the absence of the King and other senior members of the Swedish Royal Family, Prince Carl Jr. acted as host to the royal visitors during their stay.
subfiles.title: Document File Note Regarding Visit of Prince Tsunenori and Princess Toshiko to Stockholm

subfiles.about: Far Eastern Affairs officers assess diplomatic protocol regarding felicitations upon the birth of an imperial child in Japan.
subfiles.summary: An internal memorandum from the Division of Far Eastern Affairs reviewing diplomatic protocol following the birth of a Japanese imperial child. It records ceremonial officer Charles Lee Cooke's assessment that Chargé d'Affaires Edwin L. Neville must have already conveyed felicitations under standing instructions, and that no further action is necessary unless the Japanese Government issues an official notification. The author (W. T. Turner) concurs, noting that no action beyond felicitations under standing instructions was taken upon the births of earlier Imperial Princesses.
subfiles.title: Memorandum by Division of Far Eastern Affairs Regarding Felicitations for Imperial Births
